full_judgment: 10. On careful examination of the language of rule 10 it appears that undoubtedly rule 10 is prospective in operation. If the intention of the legislature was to make the provision retrospective, it would have been so clearly mentioned. In that case the period for which assessments could be reopened, would have been mentioned. In the absence of any such clear provision, the Assessing Officer is not competent to make fresh assessment for the years for which assessments were already made and tax demands already paid. In this connection the learned Advocate referred to several statutes, namely, section 34 of the Income Tax Act which provides 4 years limitation; section 28 of Sales Tax Act which provides 5 years limitation; Section 16 of the Gift Tax Act which provides 8 years' limitation; section 39 of Sea Customs Act which provides 3 months limitation; and section 15 of Business Profit Tax Act which provides 4 years limitation. The learned Advocate further submitted that Urban Immoveable Property Tax Act being a fiscal statute, in the absence of any such clear provision empowering the Assessing Officer to reopen the assessments, closed and passed, the impugned demand for those years is wholly illegal and without any lawful authority.
